card.name: The word on after nouns and verbs
card.fires_on: The word "on" (or "upon") right after a noun or verb in older, scholarly or historical prose. It often introduces a topic, subject or basis, as in "works on", "doctrine on" or "explicable on the theory".

modes.label: Topic of a work
modes.description: "on" after a noun meaning a book, doctrine or instruction, introducing its subject.
modes.example: and the various works<< on>> Egyptian antiquities.

modes.label: Verb plus on
modes.description: "on" or "upon" after a verb of motion, spending or intercession, in historical narrative.
modes.example: interceded<< on>> behalf of Artabazus and Mem

card.plain: It fires on the little word "on" when old-style writing uses it to say what a book, idea or action is about.
